children: The automaker plans to raise women’s enrolment from around 5 per cent to 30 per cent by 2028-29 to strengthen its manufacturing talent pipeline

Maruti Suzuki India plans to increase female student intake at its Japan-India Institute for Manufacturing (JIM) in Uncha Majra, Manesar, to 30% by the 2028-29 academic year, up from approximately 5 per cent in 2025-26. The initiative is aimed at building a larger pipeline of women trained for automotive manufacturing roles.

To encourage enrolment, Maruti Suzuki has introduced a 100 per cent tuition fee waiver for female students from the current academic year and plans to establish a dedicated hostel. The company also intends to increase women’s representation among faculty and support staff and strengthen the overall support system for female trainees.

The Manesar JIM offers training across nine trades, primarily focused on the automotive sector. The institutes operate under the Japan-India manufacturing skills initiative and combine classroom education with industry exposure, helping students develop practical skills relevant to manufacturing jobs.

The push comes as Maruti Suzuki has been increasing women’s participation on its manufacturing shopfloors. The company said its women workforce crossed 1,300 employees earlier this year, while more than 190 women were working directly on shopfloor roles across its Gurugram and Manesar facilities.

Maruti Suzuki operates four JIMs in India, located in Mehsana and Gandhinagar in Gujarat, and Uncha Majra and Sonipat in Haryana. The company is also planning to upgrade 31 Industrial Training Institutes to JIM standards over the next two years, with an investment of nearly Rs 100 crore, further expanding its manufacturing skills pipeline.

The initiative highlights the role of vocational education in widening women’s participation in manufacturing, where the availability of women candidates with technical training has historically been a constraint for shopfloor hiring.
